prompt.context_jp: 天天コーポレーションの経理部には、いつものように電卓のかすかな音____絶え間なく響いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 天天コーポレーションの経理部には、いつものように電卓のかすかな音____絶え間なく響いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits the scene-setting description.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence introduces a new scene by presenting what sound exists in the room — が marks this newly-perceived subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark the sound as an already-established topic, but here the sound is being introduced as part of the scenery.

contrast_examples.en: The sound of a calculator echoes (new observation).
As for the calculator sound, it's noisy (commenting on known topic).

prompt.context_jp: 訪ねる相手____山崎柊一――マイスター賞を受けた技術畑の出でありながら、営業成績でも突出した数字を叩き出す男である。
prompt.prompt_jp: 訪ねる相手____山崎柊一である。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for introducing who she's visiting?

feedback.correct_en: This is a presentational 'X は Y だ' definition: the already-mentioned 'person to visit' is the topic, and Yamazaki is the identifying predicate.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would signal brand-new subject information, but here 'the person to visit' is already set up — we're telling who that person is.

contrast_examples.en: The person (we know of) is Yamazaki.
It's Yamazaki (exhaustively) who is the one.

prompt.context_jp: しかし今日の用件____称賛ではなく、出張日程の妥当性についての静かな問い合わせだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: しかし今日の用件____称賛ではなく、問い合わせだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits here (note the 'ではなく' contrast)?

feedback.correct_en: は sets up a contrastive topic ('as for today's business, it was NOT praise but...'). The ではなく structure naturally pairs with は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would merely introduce a new subject, missing the contrastive 'not X but Y' framing the sentence requires.

contrast_examples.jp: 用件は praise ではない。
contrast_examples.en: The business is not praise (contrastive topic).
There is business (existential).

prompt.context_jp: 希梨香の手にはピンク色の試作サンプル____握られている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 希梨香の手にはピンク色の試作サンプル____握られている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: The sample is new information being introduced in the scene — が marks what is visibly held in her hand.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark the sample as an established topic, but the reader is just now seeing it for the first time.

contrast_examples.jp: サンプルが握られている。
contrast_examples.en: A sample is being held (new scene detail).
As for the sample, it's on the desk (known topic).

prompt.context_jp: 「あっ いえ 一応 責任者____山崎さんなんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 一応 責任者____山崎さんなんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Kirika is answering 'who the supervisor is.' Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: The supervisor role is the topic (just raised by Sanako). は fits a 'as for the supervisor, it's Yamazaki' answer.
feedback.incorrect_en: '責任者が山崎さんなんです' would overemphasize exhaustive identification; Kirika is simply naming the known role's filler.

contrast_examples.jp: 責任者は山崎さんです。
contrast_examples.en: The supervisor is Mr. Yamazaki (identifying topic).

contrast_examples.jp: 山崎さんが責任者です。
contrast_examples.en: Mr. Yamazaki is the one who's supervisor (exhaustive).

prompt.context_jp: 顔なじみの少ない相手を前に、彼女の声____いつもより一段低くなっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女の声____いつもより一段低くなっていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Her voice is the topic being described ('as for her voice, it was lower than usual'). は fits this characterization.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as newly-noticed, but the sentence is a reflective comment comparing to her usual state.

contrast_examples.en: Her voice is lower than usual (characterization).
Her voice trembled (observed event).

prompt.context_jp: 「年上だし 仕事できそうだなって思って 私____最初は頼りにしてたんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私____最初は頼りにしてたんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits (note the implied 'but now I don't')?

feedback.correct_en: も ('me too / even I') fits — Kirika is admitting that she, like others, initially counted on him.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just introduce a subject neutrally; を doesn't fit this verb pattern. も catches the 'I too was fooled at first' nuance.

contrast_examples.en: I too was counting on him.
I was the one counting on him (exhaustive).

prompt.context_jp: 「ラフも何もかも 馬垣さん____勝手に違うので オッケー出してたんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 馬垣さん____勝手に違うので オッケー出してたんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Kirika is revealing who did the unauthorized approval. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: が identifies the agent exhaustively — 'it was Magaki (not me) who approved it on his own.' The focus is on who did it.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make Magaki the topic for general comment, losing the accusatory 'HE was the one who did it' punch.

contrast_examples.jp: 馬垣さんがオッケーを出した。
contrast_examples.en: Magaki (is the one who) gave the OK.
As for Magaki, he often takes days off (topic).

prompt.context_jp: 「優しすぎるんですよ 山崎さん____！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 優しすぎるんですよ 山崎さん____！
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this emphatic complaint about Yamazaki?

feedback.correct_en: The right-dislocated 'Yamazaki-san は' re-establishes him as the topic being evaluated ('as for Yamazaki, he's too soft'). は fits characterizations.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like exhaustive 'it's Yamazaki (not someone else) who is too soft' — not the intended complaint.

contrast_examples.jp: 山崎さんは優しすぎる。
contrast_examples.en: Yamazaki is too kind (characterization).
Yamazaki came (event, new subject).

prompt.context_jp: 「彼____ね 逃げる男なんですよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼____ね 逃げる男なんですよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Yamazaki's warning about Magaki?

feedback.correct_en: は marks 'he' as the topic being characterized ('as for him, he's a man who runs away'). The ね also pairs naturally with topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would exhaustively identify ('HE is the one who runs away'), but Yamazaki is giving a general character assessment.

contrast_examples.en: He's the type who runs away (character).
He (specifically) ran away (event).

prompt.context_jp: 「気をつけてよ 営業____足が命なんだから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 営業____足が命なんだから。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: This is a classic 'X は Y が Z' topic-comment: 'as for salesmen, feet are their lifeline.' は sets the topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が on 営業 would make 'salespeople' a new subject, breaking the 'as for salespeople...' generalization pattern.

contrast_examples.en: Elephants have long trunks (topic-comment).
An elephant came (new subject).

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子は思わず口元____緩めかけて、慌ててその表情を引き締めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 沙名子は思わず口元____緩めかけて。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the thing being relaxed?

feedback.correct_en: 緩める is transitive — Sanako actively 'loosens' her mouth corners, so を marks the direct object.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would require the intransitive 緩む; に doesn't fit the verb's argument structure.

contrast_examples.en: Loosen one's mouth (transitive, active).
One's mouth loosens (intransitive, spontaneous).

prompt.context_jp: 「不足____9の倍数ってことは 単純な入力ミスだと思います」
prompt.prompt_jp: 不足____9の倍数ってことは 単純な入力ミスだと思います。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a subordinate 'こと' clause, が marks the subject neutrally. The whole clause 'the fact that the shortage is a multiple of 9' is the topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside this nominalized clause would awkwardly introduce a second topic layer; subordinate clauses typically use が for the subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨が降ることは知っている。
contrast_examples.en: I know (the fact) that it rains.
Rain falls (main-clause topic).

prompt.context_jp: 二人が席を立とうとした矢先、内線の電話____鋭い音を立てた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 内線の電話____鋭い音を立てた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: A sudden event with a new subject just entering the scene — が is the natural choice for 'the phone (suddenly) rang.'
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame the phone as a known topic, which doesn't match this abrupt interrupting event.

contrast_examples.en: The phone rang (sudden event).
The phone is broken (characterizing known topic).

prompt.context_jp: 街路灯____ぽつぽつと灯り始め、行き交う人の足取りには週末の気配が漂っている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 街路灯____ぽつぽつと灯り始め...
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this scene-setting?

feedback.correct_en: Scene-painting with a visible, dynamic event — が introduces the streetlights as newly-perceived subjects beginning to light up.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn the streetlights into an abstract topic rather than a visible unfolding scene.

contrast_examples.en: Cherry blossoms have bloomed (observed event).
Cherry blossoms are pretty (characterization).

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子は表情を____ず、書類の該当欄を指先でそっと示す準備を整える。
prompt.prompt_jp: 沙名子は表情を____ず、書類の該当欄を指先でそっと示す。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb completes '表情を___ず' (not letting her expression ___)?

feedback.correct_en: 表情を崩す is the set collocation meaning 'to break/lose one's composed expression.' Sanako keeps her poker face.
feedback.incorrect_en: 壊す means to physically break; 落とす doesn't collocate with 表情 in this sense.

contrast_examples.jp: 表情を崩さず応対する。
contrast_examples.en: Respond without breaking one's composure.
Break a vase (physical).

prompt.context_jp: 希梨香の不満は____を切ったように溢れ出し、店内の喧騒に紛れて延々と続いた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 希梨香の不満は____を切ったように溢れ出した。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes the idiom?

feedback.correct_en: 堰を切ったように ('like a dam breaking') is the fixed idiom for pent-up feelings or words bursting forth.
feedback.incorrect_en: 糸を切る and 幕を切る exist in other contexts but don't form this flood-of-emotion idiom.

contrast_examples.jp: 涙が堰を切ったように流れた。
contrast_examples.en: Tears flowed like a dam breaking.
To raise the curtain (start) on something.

prompt.context_jp: 「私が 1人で____で 書き直し頼んだの」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私が 1人で____で 書き直し頼んだの。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits ('apologizing profusely')?

feedback.correct_en: 平謝り (hiraayamari) is the standard word for groveling, flat-out apologizing.
feedback.incorrect_en: 大謝り and 直謝り are not established words in Japanese.

contrast_examples.en: Apologize profusely.
Apologize on one's hands and knees.

prompt.context_jp: 稟議書を巡るやり取りは、部長の一声で押し切られた形で____を閉じた。
prompt.prompt_jp: やり取りは、部長の一声で押し切られた形で____を閉じた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits ('came to a close')?

feedback.correct_en: 幕を閉じる ('to close the curtain') is the idiomatic phrase for an event/discussion coming to an end.
feedback.incorrect_en: 扉を閉じる is literal door-closing; 口を閉じる means to shut up, not to conclude a matter.

contrast_examples.en: The tournament came to a close.
Keep one's mouth shut.

prompt.context_jp: 沙名子は財布の中身を頭の中で数え、退散の頃合いを冷静に____った。
prompt.prompt_jp: 退散の頃合いを冷静に____った。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits ('gauged the right moment')?

feedback.correct_en: 頃合いを見計らう is the set collocation for 'to assess/time the right moment.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 見渡す means to survey (visually); 見つめる means to stare — neither captures timing judgment.

contrast_examples.jp: 頃合いを見計らって話しかける。
contrast_examples.en: Wait for the right moment to speak.
Survey the scenery.

prompt.context_jp: 「必要だったら いつでも書くので ____ね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 必要だったら いつでも書くので ____ね。
prompt.prompt_en: Which polite phrase fits ('please tell me')?

feedback.correct_en: 言ってください is the natural polite request. Yamazaki is being courteous but not stiff with Sanako.
feedback.incorrect_en: 申す is humble (used about oneself, not asking the other to do it); 話してやって is condescending.

contrast_examples.jp: 遠慮なく言ってください。
contrast_examples.en: Please don't hesitate to tell me.
I'll say it (humble, about self).

prompt.context_jp: 「契約書 ____早で」
prompt.prompt_jp: 契約書 ____早で。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits this business slang ('as soon as possible')?

feedback.correct_en: なる早 (naruhaya) is business shorthand for なるべく早く — 'as soon as possible.' Yoshimura uses this casually/rudely.
feedback.incorrect_en: いる早 and ある早 are not Japanese expressions.

contrast_examples.jp: なる早でお願いします。
contrast_examples.en: Please do this ASAP.

contrast_examples.jp: できるだけ早くお願いします。
contrast_examples.en: Please do it as soon as you can (fuller form).

prompt.context_jp: 一度きりと決めたこの食事だけに神経を____する――彼女はそう自分に言い聞かせて信号を渡った。
prompt.prompt_jp: この食事だけに神経を____する。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits ('concentrate one's nerves')?

feedback.correct_en: 神経を集中する is the standard collocation for focusing one's attention/nerves on something.
feedback.incorrect_en: 専念する doesn't take を on 神経; 注意する doesn't collocate this way either.

contrast_examples.en: Listen with concentrated focus.
Devote oneself to work (ni-marking).

prompt.context_jp: 押しの強さに____したのか、彼女はついに一つの短い答えを口にしようとしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 押しの強さに____したのか。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits ('overwhelmed by his persistence')?

feedback.correct_en: 根負け means to lose a battle of persistence — one's patience runs out before the other's does. Perfect for Sanako giving in.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手負け is not a standard word; 気負け means losing nerve, which is a different nuance.

contrast_examples.en: Gave in from exhaustion of resistance.
Lose one's spirit/nerve.

prompt.context_jp: Sanako wants to firmly but politely refuse the French restaurant because she has set a one-hour limit.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most like Sanako's actual blunt-but-polite style here?

choices.text: フレンチ？ 困ります 1時間で帰りたいので
フレンチ？ 嫌だ 1時間で帰る
フレンチですか？ ちょっと難しいかもしれませんね…

feedback.correct_en: The actual line uses polite ます/ので but is strikingly direct — matching Sanako's cool, business-register personality.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is too casual/rude for workplace speech; C is overly soft and indirect, which doesn't match Sanako's blunt refusal.

contrast_examples.en: That won't do (polite but firm).
I hate it (plain, blunt).

prompt.context_jp: Yamada mentions his travel allowance came through; Sanako responds flatly that she already knows.
prompt.prompt_en: Which response sounds most natural for deadpan Sanako?

choices.text: 知ってます 私が処理したので
知ってますよ 私処理しましたから
あ、そうなんですね！ よかったですね

feedback.correct_en: The crisp 'knows it because I processed it' with ので captures Sanako's professional, matter-of-fact tone perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is close but the particle-less 私処理しました sounds choppy; C would be fake-enthusiastic, totally unlike Sanako.

contrast_examples.jp: 私が処理したので知っています。
contrast_examples.en: I know because I processed it.
That's great (warm reaction — not Sanako's style).

prompt.context_jp: Sanako politely explains why she won't keep listening to Kirika's work complaints outside the office.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing best fits Sanako's polite-but-firm explanation?

choices.text: 会社以外で仕事の話をするのは 好きではないので
会社以外で仕事の話するの 嫌いだから
会社の外で働き話したくないんですよ

feedback.correct_en: The nominalized 〜のは好きではないので is measured, polite, and precise — exactly Sanako's register.
feedback.incorrect_en: B drops particles and uses blunt だから; C uses the unnatural 働き話 and sounds whiny rather than principled.

contrast_examples.en: I don't like doing 〜 (nominalized, formal).
Hate doing 〜 (casual).

prompt.context_jp: Yamada asks for 'リベンジ' (another shot) and Sanako asks what he means.
prompt.prompt_en: Which short exchange sounds most natural for this scene?

choices.text: 「リベンジさせてください」「なんのリベンジですか？」
「リベンジしたいです」「何にリベンジしますか？」
「もう一回ください」「何をもう一回？」

feedback.correct_en: させてください is the natural way to request permission; なんの+noun+ですか is the idiomatic way to ask 'what kind of X?'
feedback.incorrect_en: B's 何にリベンジ sounds unnatural — リベンジ doesn't take に like that. C drops the loanword that makes Yamada's line charming.

contrast_examples.en: What's this talk about?
What matter is this regarding?

prompt.context_jp: Sanako is leaving the izakaya before her coworkers.
prompt.prompt_en: Which parting phrase is most natural when leaving coworkers behind?

choices.text: 先に行きます、すみません
もう帰ります、バイバイ

feedback.correct_en: お先に失礼します is the standard set phrase for leaving work/colleagues before others. Sanako uses this in the actual scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is understandable but informal and awkward; C mixes casual バイバイ with coworkers, which clashes with workplace norms.

contrast_examples.en: Excuse me for leaving before you (standard).
Thanks for your hard work (reply to the above).
